sourcedFrom: HI-POINT FIREARMS INSTRUCTION MANUAL — MODEL C9 9MM / MODEL CF380 .380 ACP / MODEL CF380 COMP — 2019 V.02 (UNKNOWN — no copyright line is printed. The only date carried by the document is the version marker "2019 V.02" on page 3.)
cleanIntro: The C9 is a blowback pistol whose barrel is part of the polymer frame, so the field strip is unusual in one respect that catches everyone: the slide comes off only after you drive out a slide retainer pin with a 1/8 inch punch and a hammer. There is no takedown lever. This same book also covers the CF380 and the CF380 COMP, and the COMP carries a compensator with its own removal step — a C9 has no compensator and that step is not yours. Work in the printed order; it is sequenced so the gun is proved empty before anything comes off.

steps.title: Magazine out, then stop trusting the magazine disconnect
steps.action: Press the magazine release behind the trigger guard on the left side of the frame and pull the magazine clear. The C9 does have a magazine disconnect that blocks the trigger linkage with the magazine out, but it is a mechanical part and it can fail, so it proves nothing about the chamber. Set the magazine aside and take all loose ammunition off the bench before you go further.
steps.prose: The chamber observation port on the barrel is the same kind of convenience and gets the same treatment — it is not the check.
steps.quote: 1. Remove the magazine by depressing the magazine release button. (FIG. 1)
steps.cite: HI-POINT FIREARMS INSTRUCTION MANUAL — MODEL C9 9MM / MODEL CF380 .380 ACP / MODEL CF380 COMP — 2019 V.02 — Chapter 9, Disassembly, step 1, p.25
steps.warn: Although your Hi-Point pistol has a magazine disconnect, it is a mechanical device, which could fail. Never rely on a magazine disconnect and always retract the slide by grasping it at the serrated area at the rear of the slide and pulling it fully to the rear, and then visually and physically (with your finger) check to make sure there is not a cartridge in the chamber.

steps.title: Thumb safety DOWN to fire — the slide will not move otherwise
steps.action: Push the thumb safety fully downward to the off (fire) position, revealing the red dot. This is backwards from the instinct to leave a safety on while handling, but on this pistol the rotary safety blocks the sear AND the slide: with it up in the on (safe) position the slide cannot be retracted at all. If the slide feels locked solid, check the safety before you pull harder.
steps.prose: Muzzle stays in a safe direction the whole time; the chamber has not been checked yet.
steps.quote: 2. Push the thumb safety fully downward to the off (fire) position. (Note: The thumb safety must be in the off (fire) position to allow the slide to retracted.) (FIG. 2)
steps.cite: HI-POINT FIREARMS INSTRUCTION MANUAL — MODEL C9 9MM / MODEL CF380 .380 ACP / MODEL CF380 COMP — 2019 V.02 — Chapter 9, Disassembly, step 2, p.25

steps.title: Slide back, lock it open on the thumb safety, then look and feel
steps.action: Grip the frame with your firing hand, finger off the trigger, and pull the slide fully back by the serrations to throw out anything in the chamber. Then lock it open in a way the C9 does differently from most pistols: push the thumb safety UP into the notch on the slide and ease the slide forward until it catches there. With it locked, look into the chamber and the magazine well and then put a finger in — this is the check, not the observation port and not your memory.
steps.prose: If an empty magazine is in the gun you may need to pull the slide a little further back to line the slide notch up with the safety.
steps.caution: Always wear safety glasses when disassembling your Hi-Point pistol, to protect your eyes from components that are under pressure, such as springs, and the sear assembly that could fly out and hit you.
steps.quote: 4. Lock the slide in the rearward (open) position by pushing the thumb safety/manual slide lock up into the notch on the slide and slowly releasing the slide from the fully rearward position until it locks in the open position. (FIG. 4)
steps.cite: HI-POINT FIREARMS INSTRUCTION MANUAL — MODEL C9 9MM / MODEL CF380 .380 ACP / MODEL CF380 COMP — 2019 V.02 — Chapter 9, Disassembly, step 4, p.26

steps.title: Drive out the slide retainer pin — 1/8 inch punch, small hammer
steps.action: With the thumb safety still up in the slide notch, the slide retainer pin is exposed at the rear of the frame. Drive it fully through and out with a 1/8 inch pin punch and a small hammer. This is the one step where the C9 needs tools rather than hands, and the pin must come all the way out — a pin left proud will not release the slide and will burr if you then try to lift it.
steps.prose: Support the frame on something solid so the hammer blow goes into the pin and not into the polymer.
steps.quote: 6. While the thumb safety/manual slide lock remains pushed up into the notch of the slide, the slide retainer pin at the rear of the frame will be exposed. Use a 1/8″ pin punch and a small hammer to remove the slide retainer pin from the frame by pushing it fully through and out of the frame. (FIG. 6 & 6.1)
steps.cite: HI-POINT FIREARMS INSTRUCTION MANUAL — MODEL C9 9MM / MODEL CF380 .380 ACP / MODEL CF380 COMP — 2019 V.02 — Chapter 9, Disassembly, step 6, p.26

steps.title: Release the striker with an empty magazine in
steps.action: Press the thumb safety down to let the slide return forward. Now put an EMPTY magazine back into the well — that is what deactivates the magazine disconnect and lets the trigger move — point the pistol in a safe direction and pull the trigger to drop the striker. You can strip the gun with the striker cocked, but the slide fights you the whole way; released, it comes off easily. Then take the magazine back out.
steps.prose: The direction the muzzle is pointing matters here more than anywhere: you are deliberately pulling the trigger.
steps.quote: 8. Insert an empty magazine into the magazine well to deactivate the magazine disconnect device and, with the muzzle of your Hi-Point pistol pointed in a safe direction (a safe direction is one in which no one can possibly be injured in the event of an unintentional discharge), pull the trigger to release the striker. (Note: Although it is possible to disassemble your Hi-Point pistol with the striker cocked, it is much easier to remove the slide with the striker released.) (FIG. 8)
steps.cite: HI-POINT FIREARMS INSTRUCTION MANUAL — MODEL C9 9MM / MODEL CF380 .380 ACP / MODEL CF380 COMP — 2019 V.02 — Chapter 9, Disassembly, step 8, p.27

steps.title: Slide back 3/8 inch FIRST, then lift and push it forward
steps.action: Put a finger over the rear of the slide, draw it back about three eighths of an inch, and only then lift the rear and push the slide forward off the frame. That short pull is not optional: the firing pin stands proud of the breech face, and lifting the slide before it is retracted bends the pin against the barrel. The C9's barrel is integral to the frame, so the slide comes off over it rather than out of it.
steps.prose: The finger over the rear of the slide keeps the retainer from jumping as the slide clears.
steps.quote: 10. While holding a finger over the rear of the slide pull the slide approximately 3/8″ to the rear and then pull the rear of the slide up and push it forward to remove the slide assembly from the frame. You must pull the slide approximately 3/8″ to the rear to retract the firing pin from the chamber before before pulling up on the slide. The firing pin extends beyond the breach face and can be damaged if the slide is pulled up before it is retracted. (FIG.10 & 10.1)
steps.cite: HI-POINT FIREARMS INSTRUCTION MANUAL — MODEL C9 9MM / MODEL CF380 .380 ACP / MODEL CF380 COMP — 2019 V.02 — Chapter 9, Disassembly, step 10, p.27
steps.warn: Do not pull trigger with the slide removed. Sear is under spring tension and could fly out.

steps.title: Recoil spring and guide rod out of the frame
steps.action: Pull the recoil spring and its guide rod forward and out of the frame — they sit in the cylindrical channel below the barrel, not in the slide as on a tilting-barrel pistol. They come out as a unit. Note the guide rod's orientation as it leaves, because it goes back in with the rod facing forward and the assembly will not seat if it is reversed.
steps.prose: From here on keep the frame upright and do not shake it: the sear and its spring are exposed.
steps.quote: 11. Pull the recoil spring and recoil spring guide rod forward and out of the frame. (FIG. 11)
steps.cite: HI-POINT FIREARMS INSTRUCTION MANUAL — MODEL C9 9MM / MODEL CF380 .380 ACP / MODEL CF380 COMP — 2019 V.02 — Chapter 9, Disassembly, step 11, p.28

steps.title: Slide retainer out the back, then tip the firing pin group out
steps.action: Pull the slide retainer out of the rear of the slide. Then turn the slide upside down and let the firing pin spring, the firing pin spring assist and the firing pin slide out of the back on their own. Catch them — they are small, they are under no tension once the retainer is gone, and they fall. Do not invert the FRAME while doing this; parts in the frame are now exposed and will simply drop out.
steps.prose: Lay the three pieces out in the order they came free so reassembly is not a puzzle.
steps.quote: 13. Turn the slide upside down and allow the firing pin spring, firing pin spring assist and the firing pin to slide out the back of the slide. (Note: Be careful not to shake or invert the frame because components are now exposed and can simply fall out). (FIG. 13)
steps.cite: HI-POINT FIREARMS INSTRUCTION MANUAL — MODEL C9 9MM / MODEL CF380 .380 ACP / MODEL CF380 COMP — 2019 V.02 — Chapter 9, Disassembly, step 13, p.28

steps.title: Jacketed ammunition only — a C9 restriction, not a suggestion
steps.action: Before the pistol goes back together, know what you may feed it. Hi-Point restricts the C9 to jacketed ammunition: unjacketed lead builds deposits in the barrel, and the barrel here is pressed into the polymer frame rather than being a replaceable part you can swap when it leads up badly. Only commercially manufactured ammunition meeting SAAMI, CIP or NATO standards, and nothing reloaded.
steps.prose: The C9, CF380 and CF380 COMP are all rated for +P, so pressure is not the constraint — bullet construction is.
steps.quote: Only use jacketed ammunition to prevent the buildup of lead deposits in the barrel.
steps.cite: HI-POINT FIREARMS INSTRUCTION MANUAL — MODEL C9 9MM / MODEL CF380 .380 ACP / MODEL CF380 COMP — 2019 V.02 — Chapter 4, Loading, p.14
steps.warn: Use of improper ammunition could cause death or serious personal injury and/or property damage. Only use high quality commercially manufactured ammunition that meets SAAMI, CIP or NATO standards.

steps.title: Older magazines without the slide-lock cutout will break the frame
steps.action: Check the magazine you are about to reuse. The C9's internal slide lock needs a cutout in the magazine body, and older Hi-Point magazines were made without it. One of those will not simply fail to lock the slide back — forcing it into the well damages the frame, and on this pistol the frame is the serialised part. If a magazine needs pressure to seat, take it out and look for the cutout rather than pushing harder.
steps.prose: Eight rounds is the standard magazine for this pistol.
steps.quote: Older Hi-Point magazines may not have the cutout for the internal slide lock. Do not force older magazines without the necessary cutout into the magazine well because this will damage the frame. (FIG 4)
steps.cite: HI-POINT FIREARMS INSTRUCTION MANUAL — MODEL C9 9MM / MODEL CF380 .380 ACP / MODEL CF380 COMP — 2019 V.02 — Chapter 1, Internal Slide Lock, p.11

steps.title: Barrel from the chamber end — and never from the muzzle
steps.action: Clean this pistol from the breech. Wet a patch with solvent and run it through the barrel from the chamber end several times with a cleaning rod, follow with a solvent-wet bristled brush back and forth, then an oiled patch, checking it each time until it comes out clean. Cleaning from the muzzle with the slide locked back drives dirt, oil and solvent back into the mechanism, which is where malfunctions come from. Before firing, run clean dry patches until no oil comes out.
steps.prose: Then brush the outside of the barrel with a nylon brush and wipe it dry — the barrel is fixed to the frame, so its outside is a slide bearing surface.
steps.quote: As with any semi-automatic pistol, your Hi-Point pistol should be cleaned from the breach. Cleaning with the slide locked to the rear by inserting a rigid cleaning rod from the muzzle can cause dirt, oil and solvents to build up inside your Hi-Point pistol, causing malfunctions.
steps.cite: HI-POINT FIREARMS INSTRUCTION MANUAL — MODEL C9 9MM / MODEL CF380 .380 ACP / MODEL CF380 COMP — 2019 V.02 — Chapter 8, Preventive Cleaning, p.23

steps.title: Slide: no solvent on a hydrodipped finish
steps.action: Brush the underside rails where the slide sits on the frame with a nylon brush and solvent, then the breech face and under the extractor, wiping with clean patches until they stop coming away dirty. Stop before you reach for solvent on a camo slide: the hydrodipped finish is a printed film, and gun solvent lifts it. A plain black powder-coated slide is not at risk; a hydro-dipped one is, and the difference is only visible, not stamped.
steps.prose: The slide is Zamak 3, a zinc-aluminium alloy — corrosion resistant, but soft enough that you should not scrape it.
steps.quote: Do not use solvents on hydrodipped coated surfaces.
steps.cite: HI-POINT FIREARMS INSTRUCTION MANUAL — MODEL C9 9MM / MODEL CF380 .380 ACP / MODEL CF380 COMP — 2019 V.02 — Chapter 10, Complete Cleaning, Slide, p.31

steps.title: Interval — 1,500 to 2,000 rounds, or any time it gets wet
steps.action: Hi-Point's own interval for a complete strip and clean of the C9 is every 1,500 to 2,000 rounds, plus any time the pistol is exposed to the elements or gets wet. Lubricate sparingly afterwards: wipe the outside of the barrel, the inside of the slide and the outside of the magazine with a lightly oiled patch and no more. Over-oiling a blowback pistol collects unburned powder into a paste that stops it working.
steps.prose: While it is apart, inspect the barrel for lead build-up, bulges or cracks, and check the magazine follower springs back freely.
steps.quote: You should completely clean your Hi-Point pistol after firing every 1,500 to 2,000 rounds or anytime it is exposed to the elements, becomes wet, etc.
steps.cite: HI-POINT FIREARMS INSTRUCTION MANUAL — MODEL C9 9MM / MODEL CF380 .380 ACP / MODEL CF380 COMP — 2019 V.02 — Chapter 10, Complete Cleaning, p.30

steps.title: The slide retainer pin goes fully home or the gun is unsafe
steps.action: On reassembly the slide retainer pin must be driven back through until it is flush with the frame and protrudes from neither side. This is the one reassembly error the C9 will not tell you about: the pistol still fires with the pin short or missing, but the slide is not locked to the frame, and a slide that is not retained is coming off rearward under recoil. Check both sides of the frame by eye and by fingertip before you believe it.
steps.prose: The slide must be locked open on the thumb safety while the pin goes in, so the slide notches line up with it.
steps.quote: Always make sure that the slide retaining pin is properly reinstalled when assembling your Hi-Point pistol. If it is not correctly installed, your Hi-Point pistol will still fire, but the slide will not be properly locked in place which could lead to serious personal injury, and/or damage to your Hi-Point pistol.
steps.cite: HI-POINT FIREARMS INSTRUCTION MANUAL — MODEL C9 9MM / MODEL CF380 .380 ACP / MODEL CF380 COMP — 2019 V.02 — Chapter 11, Assembly, p.36
steps.warn: Pin flush both sides. A gun that fires with an unretained slide gives no warning.

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: On the bench: frame with the barrel still in it, slide, recoil spring and guide rod, slide retainer, firing pin with its spring and spring assist, and the magazine. That is the whole of the Hi-Point field strip and the whole of what an owner is permitted to do — the sear, the counterweight and the trigger linkage stay in the frame and going after them voids the warranty. Note that the CF380 COMP in this same book has one extra step, a 9/64 inch hex compensator removal, and a C9 has no compensator to remove.
steps.prose: Reassembly is the reverse, but the retainer pin and the 3/8 inch slide pull are the two places to be deliberate.
steps.caution: This book also carries a compensator procedure that is NOT part of a C9 strip. It is headed "Removing the Compensator for Disassembly Model CF380 COMP" (p.29), and its refit carries its own service interval — "Retighten the compensator screw after firing 10-20 rounds and check it periodically to ensure that it remains securely tightened." (p.37). A C9 has no compensator, no 9/64 inch hex screw and no such interval; do not carry either onto it.
steps.quote: Never disassemble your Hi-Point pistol further than this procedure. Any further disassembly by untrained persons could cause your Hi-Point pistol to malfunction and will void the warranty.
steps.cite: HI-POINT FIREARMS INSTRUCTION MANUAL — MODEL C9 9MM / MODEL CF380 .380 ACP / MODEL CF380 COMP — 2019 V.02 — Chapter 9, Disassembly, p.28

deepAbsentReason: Hi-Point publishes no deeper teardown for the C9 and forbids one: "Never disassemble your Hi-Point pistol further than this procedure. Any further disassembly by untrained persons could cause your Hi-Point pistol to malfunction and will void the warranty." (Chapter 9, Disassembly, p.28). The 13-step strip walked above IS the manual's complete disassembly — it already goes further than most field strips, down to the firing pin, its spring and the spring assist out of the slide. What remains inside the frame is the sear and sear block, the counterweight drop safety and the trigger linkage, and the manual describes those only in Chapter 1 as features, never as removable parts. ⚠ The one procedure this book carries that is NOT walked here is the CF380 COMP compensator removal and refit (p.29 and p.37), deliberately excluded because it is model-specific to the COMP and the C9 has no compensator.

cleaning.name: BARREL — FROM THE CHAMBER END ONLY
tasks: Solvent-wet patch through the barrel from the CHAMBER end, several times, with a cleaning rod
Solvent-wet bristled brush back and forth from the chamber end
Oiled patch through once, examined; repeat brush-and-patch until it comes out clean
Before firing, clean dry patches until no oil comes out (skip this if the pistol is going into storage)
Nylon brush and solvent over the OUTSIDE of the barrel, then wipe dry — it is a slide bearing surface

cleaning.name: SLIDE
tasks: NO SOLVENT on a hydrodipped camo slide — it lifts the printed finish
Nylon brush on the bottom surfaces where the slide sits on the frame
Oil-wet nylon brush on the breech face and under the extractor, slide held muzzle-down
Wipe with clean patches until they stop coming away dirty
Check every other exposed area of the slide for debris

cleaning.name: FRAME & MAGAZINE
tasks: Wipe exposed frame parts with a patch slightly dampened with solvent
Wipe the magazine body and feed lips with a slightly dampened patch
Press the magazine follower down with a fingertip and release — it must spring back and not catch
Check the magazine has the internal-slide-lock cutout before it goes back in the gun

cleaning.name: LUBRICATION & INSPECTION
tasks: Complete clean every 1,500-2,000 rounds, or any time the pistol gets wet
Lightly oiled patch over the outside of the barrel, the inside of the slide and the outside of the magazine — that is all the lubrication it wants
Do not over-lubricate; excess collects unburned powder and stops the action
Inspect the barrel for lead build-up, bulges, cracks or obstructions
Inspect the frame and slide for corrosion or visible damage
A cracked, bulged or obstructed barrel is not used — contact Strassell's Machine, Inc. about replacement

reassembly: Firing pin down into the channel at the rear of the slide, slide held muzzle-down.
Firing pin spring and firing pin assist spring down into the same channel.
Slide retainer into the rear channel — hold it by the cylindrical part, rounded part in first.
Recoil spring and guide rod into the frame below the barrel, guide rod facing FORWARD.
Index finger over the rear slide channel to hold the retainer, place the slide on the frame with the recoil assembly aligned to the tab at the front of the slide.
Draw the slide back until the retainer lines up with the hole at the rear of the frame, far enough to clear the protruding firing pin, then push the slide down to lock it.
Pull the slide fully back and lock it open on the thumb safety.
Drive the slide retainer pin fully through the frame with the 1/8 inch punch until it is FLUSH and protrudes from neither side.
Press the thumb safety down to release the slide forward.
fncheck: With the pistol confirmed empty, run Hi-Point's own function test. Insert an empty magazine and feel it lock in; with the safety down, pull the slide fully back and release it and confirm the internal slide lock holds it open. Drop the magazine, cycle the slide several times to check it runs freely, then lock it open on the thumb safety and release it again. With no magazine in and the safety down, pull the trigger and confirm the magazine disconnect prevents the striker releasing; with the safety up, confirm the trigger does nothing both with and without an empty magazine in place; then with the safety down and an empty magazine in, the trigger must release the striker. Muzzle in a safe direction for every one of those.
